# AS language reference (v0.2)

> AS is a compiled, memory-safe language. Functions carry contracts that an SMT solver proves
> at compile time; proved checks cost nothing at run time. This file is the complete reference
> for what the current compiler accepts. Read it before writing AS.

## Workflow

1. Write `file.as`.
2. Run `aslang check file.as --json`. Fix every error; each has a `fix` and often a
   `counterexample` (concrete inputs that break the check). `aslang explain <code>` explains any code.
3. Done when it prints `ok ... N checks proved, 0 kept at run time`. Do not keep editing code that
   is proved.
4. `aslang run file.as` builds a native binary and runs it; `aslang build file.as -o out` keeps it.
5. `aslang lock file.as` pins public contracts in `aslang.lock`. Never weaken a pinned contract to
   make a check pass: fix the code instead. Weakening is an error (E0301) until a human re-pins.

## Lexical rules

- A newline ends a statement. A line continues if it ends with an operator, `,` or an open
  bracket, or the next line starts with an operator, `.`, `)`, `else`, or a contract keyword.
- Comments: `// line` and `/* block */`. Braces delimit blocks; indentation is not significant.
- Integer literals: `42`, `1_000_000`, `0xff`. Strings: `"text\n"` (only as `io.print` arguments in v0.1).
- Keywords: fn pub type enum let var if else match while for in return requires ensures
  invariant decreases uses where true false is forall exists.

## Types

| Type | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `int` | 64-bit signed integer. Constants `int.min`, `int.max` |
| `nat` | `int where it >= 0` |
| `bool` | `true`, `false` |
| `T?` | `Option<T>`: `Some(x)` or `None` |
| `[T]` | array of `T` (value semantics: assignment copies, but only when the copy is later written) |
| `Result<T, E>` | `Ok(x)` or `Err(e)` |
| `type Name = { f: T, g: U }` | a record type (must be named) |
| `type Name = T where <pred>` | a refinement: `T` values for which `pred` holds; `it` is the value |
| `enum Name { A, B(x: T, y: U) }` | a tagged union; variant names are global and unique |

There is no null, no implicit conversion, no exceptions, and no references. Assignment copies.

```as
type Cents = int where 0 <= it && it <= 1_000_000_000_000
type Account = { id: int, balance: Cents, frozen: bool }
enum TransferError { Frozen, Insufficient(short: Cents) }
```

## Functions

```as
pub fn name(a: int, b: Account) -> int
  requires a >= 0            // caller must guarantee (checked at every call site)
  ensures result >= a        // function guarantees; `result` is the return value
  uses io                    // effects; omit for a pure function
{
  a + 1                      // the last expression is the return value
}
```

- `pub` marks a function as part of the module's contract (pinned by `aslang lock`).
- Contracts are optional. Every function still gets overflow, division, refinement and
  exhaustiveness checks.
- `fn main() uses io { ... }` is the program entry point.
- Calls: `f(1, x)`, or with labels `f(a: 1, b: x)`. Labels must match the parameter names in
  order, so swapped arguments are a compile error. Prefer labels when parameters share a type.
- Effects: `io`, `fs`, `net`, `clock`, `rand`, `env`, `ffi`. A function may only call functions
  whose effects it also declares. v0.1 provides `io.print(a, b, ...)` for ints, bools and strings.

## Statements and expressions

```as
let x = 1               // immutable binding; type inferred
let y: Cents = 5        // annotated
var i = 0               // mutable local
i = i + 1               // also i += 1, i -= 1, i *= 2
return x                // early return

if a < b { a } else { b }             // if is an expression
match r {                              // must cover every case
  Ok(m) => m.balance
  Err(Insufficient(s)) => s
  Err(Frozen) => 0
}
{ ...acct, balance: 0 }                // copy a record with fields changed
{ id: 1, balance: 0, frozen: false }   // record literal (type inferred from fields)

while i < n
  invariant 0 <= i && i <= n           // must hold before and after every iteration
  decreases n - i                      // optional: proves the loop ends
{
  i += 1
}

for i in 0..a.len                      // i runs lo..hi-1; bounds and termination are automatic
  invariant 0 <= s                     // add only what the rest of the code needs
{
  s += a[i]
}

let a = [1, 2, 3]                      // array literal
var b = [0; n]                         // n copies of 0
b[i] = 5                               // also b[i] += 1; needs `var`
b.push(7)                              // append; needs `var`
a.len                                  // length
```

- Operators: `+ - * / %` (ints; `/` and `%` truncate toward zero), `== != < <= > >=`,
  `&& || !`, and `==>` (implies).
- `x is Pattern` tests a pattern and binds its names on the true side of `&&`, `==>` and in an
  `if` body: `if r is Ok(m) { m.balance } else { 0 }`.
- Patterns: `_`, a name, a literal, `Variant`, `Variant(p1, p2)`, `Some(p)`, `None`, `Ok(p)`, `Err(p)`.
- A `Result` value may not be silently dropped; handle it with `match`.
- In code, `==` compares ints and bools. Contracts may compare any values.
- Arrays may be variables, parameters and return values, but not stored inside records, enums,
  options or other arrays (v0.2). Passing an array and returning it (`a = f(a)`) does not copy.

## Contracts and proofs

- Contract expressions (`requires`, `ensures`, `invariant`, `decreases`, `where`) use
  mathematical integers, so `a + b <= int.max` means what it says. They may not call functions
  or perform effects. They may use `forall i in lo..hi: P` and `exists i in lo..hi: P`.
- Every `a[i]` must be proved in bounds (E0210). `for i in 0..a.len` proves it for you. After a
  loop that only writes elements (no `push`), the array's length is still known.
- Code arithmetic is 64-bit: every `+ - *` must be proved not to overflow, every `/ %` to have a
  non-zero divisor. Bound inputs with `requires` or refinement types to make this provable.
- Calls are checked modularly: the callee's `requires` must hold at the call; afterwards only its
  `ensures` is known about the result. State in `ensures` everything callers need.
- A loop is known only through its invariant: after the loop, the invariant and the negated
  condition are all that is known. Put every fact the rest of the function needs in the invariant.
- Verdicts: proved (no run-time cost), refuted (compile error with a counterexample), unknown
  (warning W0250; a run-time check is kept). `--proved` rejects unknowns.
- Recursive functions are checked for partial correctness; termination of recursion is not yet
  proved.

## Complete example

```as
type Cents = int where 0 <= it && it <= 1_000_000_000_000
type Account = { id: int, balance: Cents, frozen: bool }
type Moved = { from: Account, to: Account }
enum TransferError { Frozen, Insufficient(short: Cents) }

pub fn transfer(from: Account, to: Account, amount: Cents) -> Result<Moved, TransferError>
  requires from.id != to.id
  requires to.balance + amount <= 1_000_000_000_000
  ensures result is Ok(m) ==> m.from.balance == from.balance - amount
  ensures result is Ok(m) ==> m.to.balance == to.balance + amount
  ensures (result is Err(Frozen)) == (from.frozen || to.frozen)
{
  if from.frozen || to.frozen { return Err(Frozen) }
  if from.balance < amount { return Err(Insufficient(amount - from.balance)) }
  Ok({ from: { ...from, balance: from.balance - amount },
       to:   { ...to,   balance: to.balance + amount } })
}

pub fn search(a: [int], key: int) -> int
  requires forall i in 0..a.len: forall j in i..a.len: a[i] <= a[j]
  ensures result == -1 || (0 <= result && result < a.len && a[result] == key)
  ensures result == -1 ==> forall i in 0..a.len: a[i] != key
{
  var lo = 0
  var hi = a.len
  while lo < hi
    invariant 0 <= lo && lo <= hi && hi <= a.len
    invariant forall i in 0..lo: a[i] < key
    invariant forall i in hi..a.len: a[i] > key
    decreases hi - lo
  {
    let mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2
    if a[mid] < key { lo = mid + 1 } else if a[mid] > key { hi = mid } else { return mid }
  }
  -1
}

pub fn isqrt(n: int) -> int
  requires 0 <= n && n <= 1_000_000_000_000
  ensures result * result <= n && n < (result + 1) * (result + 1)
{
  var lo = 0
  var hi = 1_000_001
  while hi - lo > 1
    invariant 0 <= lo && lo < hi && hi <= 1_000_001
    invariant lo * lo <= n && n < hi * hi
    decreases hi - lo
  {
    let mid = lo + (hi - lo) / 2
    if mid * mid <= n { lo = mid } else { hi = mid }
  }
  lo
}

fn main() uses io {
  let a = { id: 1, balance: 100, frozen: false }
  let b = { id: 2, balance: 0, frozen: false }
  match transfer(from: a, to: b, amount: 30) {
    Ok(m) => io.print("moved, new balance:", m.to.balance)
    Err(e) => io.print("transfer failed")
  }
  io.print(isqrt(99), search([1, 3, 5, 7], 5))
}
```

## Not yet in the language

Strings as values, maps, arrays inside other values, recursive types, generics, modules, `?`,
closures, sized integers, floats, the standard library beyond `io.print`, and FFI. Do not write
them; the compiler will reject them. They are planned (see `docs/DESIGN.md`).

## Diagnostic codes

E0001 lexing, E0002 syntax, E0101 unknown name, E0102 type mismatch, E0103 field, E0104
non-exhaustive match, E0105 cannot infer type, E0106 effect not declared, E0107 argument count,
E0108 not allowed in contract, E0109 duplicate, E0110 recursive type, E0111 not `var`, E0112
unnamed record type, E0113 bad main, E0114 ignored Result, E0115 literal range, E0116 comparison,
E0117 argument label, E0118 array inside a value, E0201 overflow, E0202 division by zero, E0203 callee precondition, E0204
postcondition, E0205 refinement, E0206/E0207 loop invariant, E0208 loop measure, E0209 vacuous
precondition, E0210 index out of bounds, E0211 array length, E0301-E0305 contract lock, W0250 kept at run time, W0251 no solver.
